articles.title: Hasta Marc Márquez se marea con este MotoGP
articles.standfirst: El campeón gana un Sprint de locura en su pista maldita después de que a las Aprilia les pase de todo
articles.summary: El campeón gana un Sprint de locura en su pista maldita después de que a las Aprilia les pase de todo
articles.body: Este Mundial de MotoGP 2026 es de vértigo, pasa de todo. Una montaña rusa de emociones, que dirían algunos. De hecho, hasta Marc Márquez sólo acertaba a resumirlo con un tópico que nunca caduca: “En las carreras puede pasar de todo”. Porque así fue, casi surrealista. En condiciones ‘normales’, el ilerdense habría luchado por ser quinto o sexto, pero todo se le fue poniendo de cara para que muchos también tiren de otro cliché y digan que el ‘93’ tuvo la suerte del campeón, pues ya es líder con cuatro puntos de ventaja sobre Jorge Martín. Por un lado, en la arrancada, el leridano pasaba de cuarto en parrilla a segundo, tras Martinator. Para ello, él y Di Giannantonio salieron muy bien... y cuatro máquinas hicieron el efecto acordeón, que acabó con Bezzecchi y Raúl Fernández por los suelos. El madrileño culpó al italiano de llevarlo fuera. El caso es que los dos que tenían mejor ritmo estaban KO. Para el de Cervera -y para los comisarios que no penalizaron a nadie- fue un incidente de carrera. “Fácil de explicar: cuatro motos en paralelo y yo creo que Bezzecchi estaba mirando a Raúl para frenar un poco más tarde, yo miraba a Bezzecchi, para frenar más tarde y ‘Diggia’ me miraba a mí para frenar más tarde. La consecuencia: cuatro pilotos fuera de la trazada y Martín, de quinto a primero. Fue duro y al límite, pero son carreras; la primera curva es así”, expuso. En ese lance, el del VR46, se vio frenado. “El contacto con Marc me puso la primera marcha en mi moto y ahí he perdido metros. Bezzecchi y Raúl tuvieron mala suerte”, desveló Di Giannantonio. Otros que iban más atrás, como Ogura o Acosta, levantaron y perdieron algo con el dúo español que se marchaba. Más adelante, cuando parecía que Martinator iba a ganar, el de Aprilia tuvo problemas con la presión de sus neumáticos. Para calentarlos -algo increíble, pues había 61 grados en el asfalto- se dejó pasar por Marc. “Hubo un error; unas veces es el equipo y otras, yo”, disculpaba Jorge que, cometió un fallo propio, al querer vencer al final. “Quise adelantar a Marc y me fui largo”, concedió el ‘89’. Y pasó de poder ponerse primero a verse cuarto... y ceder el liderato. “Yo esperaba perder puntos con Martín. Nuestro objetivo, y mañana es el mismo, es no perder muchos puntos. Por el momento, hoy ganamos, pero no es lo que esperábamos, pero en las carreras nunca sabes. Tienes que seguir, seguir apretando. Mañana será otra carrera, pero lo de hoy está hecho y estoy muy contento”, decía el leridano. Por cierto que el nueve veces campeón desveló que, por primera vez en su vida, se mareó tras una carrera y fue crítico con el Mundial. “Pedí agua. Fue muy intenso. Especialmente, cuando íbamos en 1:29, apreté mucho ahí. Después del podio, me sentía mareado. Nunca me pasó, pero hoy me pasó. Ya me recuperé. Es normal. Es una pesadilla hacer este podio con el mono puesto con esta temperatura. No es sólo el mono, es el ambiente, pero es lo que hay. Por eso intento cuidarme, porque somos atletas y queremos rendir lo mejor posible. En una moto, para rinda mejor, la cuidas de la mejor manera, la enfrías y todo eso. Conmigo debo hacer lo mismo. Por eso, salté del carrito de golf y me fui a mi oficina para intentar recuperarme”, confesó antes de lanzar otro dardo: “Diez minutos obligatorios en el ‘Hero walk’ (paseo con los fans), siempre un poquito más. Es lo que hay y tenemos que hacerlo”. Este MotoGP es tan alucinante que lo más probable es que Aprilia arrase en la carrera larga y el del Ducati oficial sufra, que ‘Bez’ y Raúl se escapen. O que Martín recupere el liderato, pero con Marc Márquez ya nunca se sabe. Ni en su circuito maldito.

articles.title: Cesarewitch: Alphonse Le Grande edges Sea Lantern for historic Newmarket win
articles.summary: Tony Martin's Alphonse Le Grande repeated his heroics of 2024 by taking home top honours in the Godolphin Cesarewitch Handicap at Newmarket, becoming just the second horse to win the race twice; The winner, ridden by Patrick McGettigan, denied Sea Lantern in a photo finish
articles.body:
The Tony Martin-trained seven-year-old stayed on strongly under 5lb claimer Patrick McGettigan to cut down 4-1 favourite Sea Lantern who had hit the front with less than a furlong to run, with the winner landing the historic handicap by a short head. The well-backed Dawn Rising, runner-up 12 months ago, was third, with High Fibre fourth.

The victory repeated Alphonse Le Grande's 2024 win, seeing him emulate Aaim To Prosper who won the race in 2010 and 2012.

Martin - who was serving a three-month suspension which meant Cathy O'Leary held the licence when Alphonse Le Grande struck two years ago - said: "I couldn't believe it, I thought we had ruined our chances by running two weeks ago at the Curragh. But he's such a tough little horse he pulled it out the bag. He keeps turning up when we need him and on better ground he finds another gear.

"I didn't know we had got it, but I'm delighted he got the right result in the photo - I just need to make sure the jockey weighs in!

"He has never ridden for me before, but he came up and sat on him in the week and I loved the positivity. He did exactly what we asked him to do when we had a good chat with him in the week.

"He rode in the race last year and for a fellow of his age he really shone there today. I was hoping it would happen, but you can never be sure a 5lb claimer would be capable of doing that and he was excellent.

"I knew they had started racing early and I wondered had he overdone it a little bit, but we were tracking the right man turning in and he was a length off Ryan Moore and it was great for a young lad to have the patience to do what he did."

He added: "I thought the ground was gone two years ago when he won and I probably shouldn't have run him at the Curragh last time. But he's such a tough and durable horse and he's bounced back. Luckily the weather has held, he got his ground today and we got a great result.

"He's only seven and if he comes home safe and sound we can have plenty of fun with him again next year."

For Brian Ellison it was a bittersweet result, as Sea Lantern returned defeated but with his Malton handler dreaming of bigger days ahead.

He said: "He's run an unbelievable race and he got a bump which I'm not sure if it cost him. He's run brilliant.

"He's a really good horse and I think he could definitely be a Group horse. He's so laid-back, it's gutting we got beat but we're so pleased he ran so well."

articles.title: Alonso cambia otra vez el motor y deberá salir desde el 'pit lane'
articles.standfirst: Tras la falta de potencia en el sprint y la qualy, Honda le cambia la unidad de potencia que estrenó en Bakú. Ha durado menos de tres GP.
articles.summary: Tras la falta de potencia en el sprint y la qualy, Honda le cambia la unidad de potencia que estrenó en Bakú. Ha durado menos de tres GP.
articles.body: Fernando Alonso correrá con un motor nuevo, según ha confirmado Honda F1 tras la calificación del GP de Singapur. El asturiano se quejó de la falta de potencia en las rectas, que según arrojó la telemetría le hacía perder hasta 1,2 segundos por vuelta en el sprint. Así, en principio debería salir al fondo de la parrilla, o mejor dicho, desde el pit lane, cuando había sido 16º en la qualy. "La lluvia justo antes de la carrera sprint provocó condiciones de pista mojada, lo que creó un escenario desafiante para la gestión de la energía. A pesar de los obstáculos, logramos recopilar datos valiosos durante la sesión", decía Honda en su comunicado oficial. "Analizamos esa información y trabajamos para optimizar los ajustes de cara a la clasificación. Aunque el resultado no fue la posición que buscábamos, seguimos profundizando en el conocimiento del paquete técnico bajo las condiciones particulares que hemos afrontado este fin de semana", añadía. Finalmente, confirmaban la noticia, "Tras los comentarios de Fernando durante la clasificación, hemos decidido sustituir la unidad de potencia durante la noche (del sábado al domingo). Aún queda mucho trabajo por hacer antes de la carrera de mañana, pero el equipo mantendrá la concentración en la tarea y seguirá preparándose para el Gran Premio". La rotura del régimen de parque cerrado impide a cualquier coches salir desde la parrilla de salida y deberá hacerlo desde la calle de boxes. Este motor sería el de la spec 2B de 2026, es decir, en que tiene la segunda mejora del ADUO, que se introdujo en Bakú y que cuenta con un turbo mejorado. Allí en Azerbaiyán, una fuga de aceite obligó a quitarlo para el sábado y colocarlo otra vez arreglado para el domingo, donde Fernando salió desde el pit.. Alonso se retiró de aquella carrera por falta de potencia, aunque Honda no vio nada de nada en los datos, pese a que el asturiano estaba seguro de que no estaba bien. En Sepang le permitió llegar hasta su mejor resultado de la temporada, con el octavo, y durante este fin de semana en Singapur, regresaron los problemas de falta de potencia.

articles.title: Singapore Grand Prix: Max Verstappen builds major momentum as 'no-one very happy' at McLaren after bad day at office
articles.summary: Max Verstappen's revival might not be a serious issue for Kimi Antonelli but it is for McLaren, who had a bad Saturday in Singapore, writes Andrew Benson.
articles.body:
Max Verstappen is too far behind, and Kimi Antonelli too far ahead, to consider that Red Bull's revival might create any real jeopardy in the championship fight - but the Dutchman is certainly building some major momentum as the Formula 1 season moves into its closing stages.

Verstappen finished Saturday in Singapore with pole position for the grand prix to add to the sprint-race victory he had completed in tricky wet conditions earlier in the day.

And that gives him a great opportunity to complete a second grand prix victory within a week if he can convert on Sunday.

Verstappen has two eager Ferrari drivers right behind him, after Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton both felt that they had just missed out on a pole position that was possible.

He also has concerns about Red Bull's inconsistent starts - he lost the lead off the line both in Malaysia last weekend and in the sprint.

If he does drop back at the start in Singapore, it is the sort of track where overtaking is at a premium and he will not find it as easy to get back in front as he did on his way to his first victory of the season.

And he is, as one would expect, not getting ahead of himself.

"It was a good qualifying," Verstappen said. "It was always very close and we got ahead when it mattered and we are very happy with that.

"All weekend the car has been in a good window and that makes it a lot easier to find your rhythm. Incredibly happy to start first. Still a long race ahead, a lot of things can go wrong but we have done everything up until now well so hopefully we can continue that tomorrow.

"It's been a really positive last few races and we want to keep that momentum going."

Verstappen beats Ferraris to Singapore pole

Verstappen wins sprint after Russell crashes out

Verstappen's maiden win of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend came after a run of three podium finishes in Italy, Spain and Azerbaijan, the last of which might very well have been a first victory had he not had problems in qualifying that left him eighth on the grid when he could have been on the front row.

His upturn in form has come as a result of steady work from Red Bull in improving their car and getting it into a position where he feels he can predict its behaviour and therefore push to the limit.

When a Red Bull is in that spot, Verstappen can be close to unbeatable.

He proved that in his remarkable comeback last year, when he gave McLaren and Lando Norris nightmares with a quite brilliant second half of the season that saw him eat into a 100-point deficit to the championship lead and ultimately miss out on taking a fifth title by just two points.

This year, Verstappen's deficit to Antonelli is even bigger than that.

He is 129 points behind the Mercedes driver with only 175 still remaining, assuming the two end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi do actually take place in the context of the war in the Middle East.

It would take some kind of miracle - involving not only a non-stop stream of wins for Verstappen and a highly unlikely run of poor form and bad luck for Antonelli - for him to turn that around. So the prospect can be realistically dismissed.

But he certainly looks as if he will be a contender at the front for the remainder of the season.

If that is not a major concern for Antonelli, it certainly is for McLaren.

They had their own purple patch in the summer, when Lando Norris took consecutive wins in Hungary and the Netherlands, and would have won in Madrid had it not been for the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car.

But the world champions have slipped from competitiveness in recent races, and before the Singapore Grand Prix they lie in third place in the constructors' championship, only 11 points ahead of Red Bull.

Saturday in Singapore was a bad day at the office for McLaren.

Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were heading for fourth and fifth places in the sprint when Norris made a dive down the inside of his team-mate at Turn Five on the final lap.

This is not a common overtaking spot and from a McLaren point of view it was a move with no reward, only risk.

The move might have made sense if it had come earlier in the race and enabled Norris to challenge Leclerc, struggling in front of them, for third.

But on the last lap, Norris was not going to have a go at Leclerc even if he had got through - the only remaining overtaking place was at the end of the following straight into Turn Seven.

If the McLaren drivers swapped places, it would make no difference to the team in terms of a collective points haul, but if it went wrong, the cost could be high.

And so it did. Norris was in a position to make a legitimate move, but they came together, pirouetted in tandem, Piastri into the barriers and out of the race and Norris slipping down to eighth. Nine points had become one.

The stewards took no action, feeling that "both drivers had contributed to the incident".

Piastri had explained in the hearing that he did not expect Norris to try a move there, and attempted to leave space when he saw him.

Norris argued that his his car was in a position that, according to the rules, entitled him to make an overtaking attempt, so expected to be left space and had braked and gone over the kerb when he realised he was not going to get as much as he expected.

He said: "There are two sides, one is what the stewards say and that's a fair reasoning, no-one's to blame. But I did apologise because it was still me attacking, as I had the right to do. If I just sat there and was boring like I should be, nothing would have happened. So really it's still my fault but I deserved to go for the space and I still believe I had the right for it."

Norris added: "As you probably expect, no-one's very happy. I'm not happy, Oscar isn't happy. None of us wanted it to go that way. There was things both of us could have done better and, yeah, we spoke about it and we moved on."

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

Team principal Andrea Stella is a measured man who chooses his words carefully, but his displeasure was clear.

"It was a very long, tiring and challenging day," he said. "Very simply, it is unacceptable that two McLarens ever come together on track. This is a fundamental principle of how we go racing, and something both drivers are very well aware of.

"As always, we discuss these incidents as a team in a constructive and productive way as there is always something to learn and take forward to emerge stronger. These are not conversations we need to have in public, but we have reminded our drivers that the interests of the team must always come first, and that did not happen today."

The context for the collision comes after two seasons where Norris and Piastri have had a number of incidents that created tensions, especially in their title battle last season. Lessons do not appear to have been learned in the way Stella might have expected.

Stella said he was "disappointed" more than anything, pointing out that this was far from the first conversation he had had with the drivers on the need to put the team's interests first.

"We as a team need to reflect as to how we make sure that these situations do not happen any more," he said.

"It is serious. It is serious because the damage for the team is material. We are in a close fight in the championship.

"We had the ambition to challenge Ferrari and this is a problem in the challenge for the second position, and we have an ambition to finish ahead of Red Bull, and this is a problem to finish ahead of Red Bull.

"And it is also serious because we come from a few seasons in which we have reflected together, team and drivers, as to how we approach racing together and how we make sure that the interest of the team is protected.

"It is serious, but at the same time we approach it with a very constructive mindset because there is only one outcome, that the team will be more united and the team will be stronger in the way we pursue our quest, which is the drivers' and the team's quest, together."

articles.title: Singapore GP: Can Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton work together to beat Max Verstappen in Sunday's race?
articles.summary: Pole-sitter Max Verstappen is set to have a race-long battle against Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in Singapore; watch Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix at 1pm (build-up from 11.30am) live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Verstappen will start on pole for the second weekend in a row with Charles Leclerc on the front row and Hamilton in behind in third, with all three drivers desperate to win their second races of 2026.

The tight confines of the Marina Bay Street Circuit means overtaking is difficult so the start will be crucial when the lights go out at 1pm (build-up from 11.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 .

"As a team we need to do whatever it takes to win," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 .

"The start in the Sprint was in the wet so it was different. But I believe from third we can have a good start. I will try to capitalise there and after that I think we have a car we can fight with.

"I will give it absolutely everything to try and undo our qualifying. It would be great for us to get another win."

Having topped Q1 and Q2 in Qualifying, Hamilton headed into Q3 as favourite but could not put a completely clean lap together so was beaten by Verstappen and Leclerc by just one tenth.

"The car felt amazing in Q1 and Q2, and when I finished the laps, I was like, 'she's got more in her'. And the only way in order to try and extract that is to try and add wing," he explained.

"In doing so, I think it just tipped it over the edge. It was only like one hole or something like that, but it was just on the knife point, and after that then the car was just snappy, and none of the laps in Q3 are any good. So I'm grateful to be third, to be honest, given that those laps weren't very good."

How vulnerable is Verstappen at the start?

Verstappen is concerned about the start after a "horrendous" launch in Saturday's Singapore Sprint which saw him lose out to George Russell before the Mercedes driver crashed at the end of the lap.

It was reminiscent of last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but both starts were in the wet and Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix is expected to be dry.

However, even Verstappen's most recent starts have not been good in comparison to his rivals. Although he did not lose positions by the end of the first lap in the last three dry starts in Baku, Madrid and Monza, his initial getaway off the line was, at best, average in all three Grands Prix and he was forced to fight hard into Turn 1 itself to retain his starting position.

Given the first corner in Singapore does not require the drivers to brake hard, Verstappen will not be able to recover from a poor getaway on Sunday, particularly if the Ferraris start quickly.

"That's definitely something that we need to improve on because if you have something like that tomorrow, that's your race over if nothing crazy happens," said Verstappen, who will make his 250th F1 start.

"We have a few limitations that we have to work on. Also from our side, I think we have to do a better job, because Racing Bulls sometimes do start better than us. So we just need to be better."

Leclerc and Hamilton themselves will be itching to get away cleanly and will be aware of the importance to be the leading Ferrari after the first lap.

It might mean the two Ferraris get very close on the short run down to Turn 1 and both drivers are likely to be unwilling to back out...

What can happen after the start in Singapore?

The high Singapore track temperatures coupled with several traction zones mean tyre degradation can be an issue during the long race, which often can get close to the two-hour limit due to the relatively low average speed.

However, the drivers have learned, if they manage their pace, you can stretch the first stint length to make a one-stop race work.

"In terms of strategy we will have to look, but it's also true whoever is behind after the first lap, if that happens, the second car can lose a lot - whether that's Lewis or me," Leclerc told Sky Sports F1 .

"That's a team choice and something we will discuss. If a win is on the table we will have to take a decision. But we will talk about it."

Leclerc is suggesting the second Ferrari will need to try something different, or perhaps even sacrifice themselves by helping the other car.

The two options the second Ferrari would have is to pit relatively early to try and undercut Verstappen, if needed, allowing the leading car to have free air. Or to run long and hope for a timely Safety Car or Virtual Safety Car to make a 'cheaper' pit stop where you lose less time in the pits compared to pitting under green flag conditions.

"It will be very hard for us to beat Max tomorrow, but there's two Ferraris there and I think we can hopefully, there might be opportunities for us to work together to try and apply the pressure," said Hamilton.

"They [Red Bull] are very quick but I think we have the car in a good place that hopefully we can at least hold on."
